name: Biwakplatz
beschreibung:
Overview

The entry named Biwakplatz cannot be assigned to any specific, officially registered camping or bivouac establishment in Tyrol. The term generally refers to a simple overnight spot for mountain tours and not to an individual facility with an address, opening hours or contact person. In Tyrol, camping – i.e. people spending the night in tents, caravans, motor vehicles, motorhomes, mobile homes and similar mobile accommodation as part of tourism – is generally prohibited outside campsites. Only bivouacking in high alpine terrain remains permitted, understood as a one-off, makeshift overnight stay during a mountain tour, for example in the event of a sudden turn in the weather, injury or darkness.

History/Background

The legal basis in Tyrol is the Tyrolean Camping Act 2001 (Act of 21.03.2001 on the regulation of camping in Tyrol). It prohibits camping outside approved campsites and permits only bivouacking in high alpine terrain as well as camping by order of the mayor in the event of local need. The construction or substantial modification of a campsite must be notified in writing to the district administrative authority. In addition, the following applies throughout Austria: camping in the forest is prohibited under the Forest Act 1975, since free access to the forest expressly does not include staying overnight in the dark or pitching a tent.

Getting there

Since no address can be clearly verified for this entry, no specific travel routes, public transport or parking options can be reliably stated either. In addition, the coordinates stored in the dataset lie outside Tyrol and therefore do not match a Tyrolean location. A reliable description of how to get there is not possible on this basis. Anyone wishing to spend the night in Tyrol should turn to an officially approved campsite and check access using the information provided by the respective establishment or the local municipality.

Tips

Planned, intentional bivouacking is treated legally like a night in a tent and can be punished as an administrative offence. In protected areas – such as national parks, nature and special protection areas or quiet zones – as well as on fields and in forests, camping may be entirely prohibited under certain circumstances. Hikers and mountaineers should inform themselves before a tour with the competent district administrative authority or protected area management about local rules, use resources sparingly and take waste back with them. For a regular overnight stay, using an approved campsite is the safe route.

Best time to travel

For mountain tours and alpine activities in Tyrol, the snow-free summer months are generally suitable, while high alpine terrain often retains patches of snow into early summer and in winter is accessible only to experienced mountaineers with appropriate equipment. Since it is not a specific establishment, no verifiable opening or season period can be given; the general seasonal conditions of the respective mountain range apply.
